subject.title: fix(agents): map cacheRetention 'standard' to 'short' for Bedrock Claude models

question: Should OpenClaw support `cacheRetention: "standard"` as an Anthropic-family config alias, or should existing/default configs be normalized to the existing `none | short | long` contract?
rationale: Both paths can fix the user problem, but they create different public config contracts and upgrade behavior, and automation should not choose that policy for maintainers.

options.title: Align and support the alias
options.body: Document and type `standard` as a compatibility alias for eligible Anthropic-family providers, keep the resolver mapping, and land one canonical PR.

options.title: Keep the current contract
options.body: Reject or migrate `standard` through defaults, validation, or doctor repair so runtime continues to accept only `none | short | long`.

options.title: Accept runtime-only compatibility
options.body: Land a hidden alias deliberately, accepting that docs and exported types will not describe every accepted runtime value.

recommendation.title: Keep the current contract
recommendation.body: Reject or migrate `standard` through defaults, validation, or doctor repair so runtime continues to accept only `none | short | long`.

likelyOwner.reason: The path history ties steipete to the resolver extraction and related cache-retention/default contract surfaces, making this the best available owner for the config-contract choice.
